published.citation: Cabot et al. 2021, dayside brightness temperature in the TESS band, assuming zero geometric albedo: 3237 +/- 59 K, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162..218C/abstract

temperature.note: Its day side's brightness temperature is measured in secondary eclipse in the TESS band (TESS) and nobody has imaged it, so the color is a Planck spectrum at its published temperature.
temperature.chosen: the paper's own value, from a TESS eclipse 364 ± 28 ppm deep; no infrared eclipse is published
